authorization_note: Preparation only. Admin token access does not authorize these changes; apply only on an explicit owner order.

requests.notes: contexts re-derived from check-runs on main HEAD; 'receiver' is the only context that exists on main today. 'runtime-config' is integration-branch-only and must NOT be added until its check-run appears on a main SHA. strict and enforce_admins are explicit owner-reversible choices. All other fields null = no rule; nothing else is configured.
requests.preserve: No prior protection object exists (verified 404); nothing to merge.

requests.notes: Free on public repos; admin token confirmed. Non-provider patterns, validity checks and Dependabot deliberately omitted — out of scope, not denied as unsupported.
requests.preserve: Only the two named statuses are touched; other security_and_analysis keys are left as-is by PATCH semantics.

stale_plan_conditions: Required contexts are bound to check-runs on fd5ff804. If main's ci.yml gains or renames jobs (e.g. runtime-config after the integration merge), re-GET check-runs on the then-current main SHA and rebuild contexts before applying.
If a branch protection object or ruleset is created meanwhile, PUT protection overwrites whole-object — re-GET and merge into the existing rules instead of applying verbatim.
If the repo becomes private, secret scanning/push protection may need GitHub Advanced Security; a PATCH 403 then is a plan limit, not a payload bug.
If org-level rulesets appear (re-run rulesets?includes_parents=true), org rules may already impose checks; reconcile before adding repo protection.
If the 'receiver' job is renamed, the stale context silently blocks all merges — detect via check-runs on a fresh main SHA.
strict:true presumes no merge queue; if the repo adopts a merge queue, switch to the merge-queue-aware protection fields instead.
post_apply_readback: GET /repos/.../branches/main/protection -> required_status_checks.strict true, contexts ['receiver'], enforce_admins.enabled true.
GET /repos/... -> security_and_analysis.secret_scanning.status 'enabled' and secret_scanning_push_protection.status 'enabled' (enablement can be eventual; re-GET once if 'enabling').
GET /repos/.../rulesets?includes_parents=true -> record any ruleset that appeared; reconcile with the protection object.
Enforcement proof still needs one real merge attempt on a PR missing 'receiver' — configuration GETs alone do not prove the gate.
